acv.quote: A hundred and eighty K a year, on a three-year term.

header.reason: A Fetchwell engineer built a working sitter payment flow in our sandbox over a weekend, and Daniel stopped saying 'if.' Priya calls it clean, but the PayPal, Venmo and saved-card questions stayed open.

findings.label: What started it
findings.finding: Aim messaging at companies expanding abroad that must pay workers locally.
findings.why: Fetchwell was launching Canada and the UK, while two engineers just kept sitter payments working.
findings.quote: sitters have to get paid locally

findings.label: Who decided
findings.finding: Win over the engineering lead with something his team can build fast.
findings.why: Daniel signed. The CFO joined one call for ten minutes and asked one question.
findings.quote: this is an engineering decision, finance will sign what I bring them

findings.label: The competitor
findings.finding: Have a clear answer ready on keeping PayPal and Venmo buttons.
findings.why: After Fetchwell met Braintree, their questions turned to what they'd lose. Priya only guesses Braintree caused it.
findings.quote: It went from 'how fast can we build this' to 'what do we lose.'

findings.label: Our message
findings.finding: Swap the acceptance-rate slide for the docs and sandbox story.
findings.why: Daniel shrugged off the average approval gain. The sandbox got a Fetchwell engineer building on her own time.
findings.quote: I'm not losing sleep over auth rates

findings.label: Missing proof
findings.finding: Find a customer of similar size who moved saved cards without losses.
findings.why: Daniel asked for this, Priya promised to get back to him, and never did.
findings.quote: who's done this at our size without losing cards?

findings.label: Their words
findings.finding: Say 'sitter pay' and 'paid by Friday' instead of 'payouts.'
findings.why: Fetchwell's whole promise to sitters is pay by Friday, and nobody there says payouts.
